findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete rule the skill uses to classify a tracker as 'the project's own mandated tracker' (un-gated writebacks) vs. 'third-party' (approval-gated), so the gate distinction is mechanically applicable and reconciles with the existing Approval-gate rule at SKILL.md L99-100.
evidence: Plan: "the project's own mandated tracker gets prescribed writebacks; third-party trackers stay approval-gated"
Existing invariant SKILL.md:100: "including but not limited to: writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers" is approval-gated
ABSENCE: no criterion given for how the running agent decides which side of the gate a given tracker falls on — the distinction is load-bearing for whether the fail-safe is preserved or breached
findings.finding: The writeback approach hinges on classifying a tracker as 'the project's own mandated tracker' (prescribed, un-gated writebacks) vs. 'third-party' (approval-gated), but the plan states no rule the agent can apply to make that determination in an arbitrary client project — and it silently amends the existing hard fail-safe (SKILL.md L99-100 gates 'writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers').
findings.location: Approach, change (14) 'Approval-gate reconciliation'; against SKILL.md L99-100
scenarios: Client project uses rebar AND a corporate Jira; agent must decide which gets auto-writebacks and which stays gated
A project where rebar itself is not the 'mandated' tracker — the agent cannot tell which tracker to auto-write to
findings.suggested_fix: Define the discriminator inline (e.g., the tracker the skill is already operating within / the one that produced the ticket under debug is the 'own mandated tracker'; any other named tracker is third-party), and add an explicit sentence amending the Approval-gate section so it does not contradict the prescribed writebacks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the discriminator the skill uses to classify a tracker as the project's own mandated one vs third-party (e.g. tracker declared in the project's own config/workflow = mandated; otherwise gated).
evidence: 'the project's own mandated tracker gets prescribed writebacks; third-party trackers stay approval-gated'
The plan states the intended split but not the observable signal the skill uses to classify a tracker as 'own mandated' vs 'third-party'
findings.finding: The approval-gate reconciliation distinguishes 'the project's own mandated tracker' (gets prescribed writebacks) from 'third-party trackers' (stay approval-gated), but the plan does not state how the executing skill DECIDES which tracker a given project's is — leaving the discriminator to the executor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause defining the test, e.g.: 'the project's own mandated tracker' = the tracker the project's configured workflow requires; absent such a declaration, treat as third-party and apply the approval gate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the two Step-7 triggers compose (e.g. enter Step 7 if EITHER the root cause is a repeatable construct OR the fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces), so the parity axis is not gated out by the existing repeatable-pattern trigger.
evidence: Existing gate SKILL.md:555: "Run this only when the root cause is a repeatable pattern"
Plan describes parity siblings as "ABSENCES invisible to grep" — i.e. not repeatable constructs
ABSENCE: plan does not state whether Step 7 is entered if EITHER trigger fires (construct-recurrence OR parallel-surface), leaving axis-2 potentially gated out
findings.finding: Change 15 adds a second Step-7 axis with its own trigger ('only when fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces'), but Step 7 as written is entered only under the existing trigger ('Run this only when the root cause is a repeatable pattern', SKILL.md L555). A parity sibling is an ABSENCE on a parallel surface — not a recurring construct — so under the existing gate the new axis is skipped exactly when it applies. The plan does not state how the two triggers compose at the single Step-7 entry point.
findings.location: Approach, change (15) 'Trigger: only when fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces'; against SKILL.md L555
scenarios: A one-site fix on a shared core with parallel CLI/MCP/library surfaces but no recurring construct: repeatable-pattern trigger is false, so Step 7 (and thus axis-2) is skipped and the parity sibling is missed
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the Step-7 entry so each axis carries its own independent trigger and the step is entered when either fires; run axis-1 when its trigger holds and axis-2 when its trigger holds.

Alternative differs structurally at the control-flow/gate boundary: prescribe content, keep the human-approval step for the mutation
Existing skill already leans strongly fail-safe on tracker mutation (SKILL.md L99-105), which the content-only alternative aligns with
findings.finding: An alternative writeback approach is not weighed: keep the existing approval gate intact for ALL trackers and make change 14 supply only the PRESCRIBED CONTENT of each writeback (agent drafts the RCA/summary/classification comment; user approves the mutation). This removes the load-bearing tracker-classification problem entirely and preserves the skill's existing fail-safe posture at lower blast radius.
scenarios: Any client project where 'own vs third-party tracker' is ambiguous — the content-only alternative works with no classification needed
